prompt.es: Escribe tu borrador (110–190 palabras) sobre el mercado.

answer.text: On balance, I think moving the market is probably a mistake. According to the local paper, traders are said to have lost half their income during the trial week, and a survey claims that sixty per cent of residents prefer the current site. Although the council has a point about traffic, a car park may well hurt the town centre more than it helps. Shops nearby need the crowds that the market brings. Having listened to both sides, I would support a short trial at the new site, as long as the traders are consulted first. If the trial went badly, we would return to the old site, and the council would have to publish the results. In that way, everybody would know what happened, and the plan could be improved before any final decision.
accepted: On balance, I think moving the market is probably a mistake. According to the local paper, traders are said to have lost half their income during the trial week, and a survey claims that sixty per cent of residents prefer the current site. Although the council has a point about traffic, a car park may well hurt the town centre more than it helps. Shops nearby need the crowds that the market brings. Having listened to both sides, I would support a short trial at the new site, as long as the traders are consulted first. If the trial went badly, we would return to the old site, and the council would have to publish the results. In that way, everybody would know what happened, and the plan could be improved before any final decision.

In my opinion, moving the market would probably do more harm than good. The local paper reports that traders are said to have lost half their income in one week, and a survey claims that most residents prefer the present site. Even though the council has a point about traffic, a car park may well damage the town centre. Many shops nearby need the crowds that the market brings. After hearing both sides, I would accept a short trial at the new site provided that the traders are consulted first. If the trial went badly, we would go back to the old site, and the council would have to publish the results. That way, everyone would know what happened, and the plan could be improved before the final decision.
